newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil cargo premiums firm, barge heat slips.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil cargo premiums firm, barge heat slips.

text.p: Steady demand and lack of shipping strengthened premiums for NWE low sulphur gas diesel cargoes on Tuesday but slack German buying interest eroded premiums for heating oil barges, traders said.
Volume was thin due to a lack of vessels and a slide in futures that inspired caution in physical markets, they said.
Benchmark Feb IPE gas oil futures eased $4 to $205 a tonne at 14.30 GMT weakness and milder weather across Europe and the United States which is due to continue for some days.
French heating oil premiums are steady, bid into Bordeaux at Feb +$14 before the end of January to cover a short position.
But no sellers have emerged. German winter heating oil was offered $1 easier at Feb +$6. Prompt Russians were Feb +$7.50 cif NWE.
Low sulphur diesel was steady on good demand, bid at Feb +$22 prompt cif Le Havre on Tuesday after an Algerian traded at Feb +$21 on Monday.
Barges were thinly traded, with heating oil sliding $1.50 on meagre demand caused by ice that blocked canal deliveries.
Refinery grade heating oil traded at Feb +$6 prompt fob ARA. Feburary was done at Feb +$4. Low sulphur diesel gained $1, with prompt material done at Feb +$13.50 fob ARA.
